cohort: 112 patients with singleton vaginal deliveries complicated by OASIS, selected from a total of 12,081 vaginal deliveries at King Abdulaziz University Hospital between 2017 and 2020, excluding preterm births and incomplete records.
finding: The incidence of Obstetric Anal Sphincter Injuries (OASIS) was 0.93% and showed a decreasing trend from 2017 to 2020, with Grade III tears being the most common (79.5%) and higher estimated blood loss associated with Grade IV cases.
mod_finding: N/A (The study reported the prevalence of spontaneous vaginal delivery among OASIS cases but did not present a specific finding on the association between mode of birth and OASIS risk or severity.)
